tower.money.in.held.refuseBody: Nothing has been credited for {ref}, so nothing is taken back. The shop’s request waits for a payment again.
tower.money.in.held.credited: Credited — it was on the statement.
tower.money.noLedgerBody: No fee, top-up or payout has been recorded.
tower.support.title: Find a parcel
tower.support.lede: Somebody is on the phone or at a counter. One number, and the parcel’s whole story.
tower.support.placeholder: Parcel sticker ID, or a load’s barcode or code
tower.support.emptyBody: Type the number from the sticker. This is not a search of the network — the person you are talking to already has the number.
tower.support.noScans: This parcel has no journey recorded yet.
tower.support.heardLate: done with no signal, dated by the phone · reached us {at}
tower.support.papersSeen: crosses a border · papers seen at the counter {at}
tower.support.papersNotSeen: crosses a border · papers not looked for yet
tower.money.personRefund: Owed back to a person: what their door delivery did not use
tower.withdraw.hint: A person’s parcel that has gone no further than a hub can be withdrawn. You are told first what that would do.
tower.withdraw.voidBooked: It was never handed in: it is withdrawn, and nothing was paid for it.
tower.withdraw.voidAtShop: It has not left {shop}: it is withdrawn there, and the shop gives back what was paid at its counter.
tower.withdraw.turnRound: It is at {hub}. It goes back to {shop}, the shop it was handed in at, as a new parcel to its sender, who pays {amount} in cash there as they collect it. What was carried to the hub is not given back. The sender and the receiver are told in their app, where they have one; the hub puts a new label on it.
tower.withdraw.doneTurned: Turned round: it goes back to {shop} as {id}
tower.withdraw.comesBackAs: Withdrawn at a hub: it goes back to its sender as {id}.
tower.withdraw.takesBack: It takes {id} back to its sender, withdrawn at a hub.
tower.withdraw.takesBackDue: It takes {id} back to its sender, withdrawn at a hub. {amount} is due in cash at the counter as they collect it.
tower.support.reissueHint: The only way back from a code guessed to death. A parcel never carries its own release key and the shop handing it over never learns it — so nobody can read the old one out, and this replaces it rather than revealing it.
tower.support.sentTitle: A new code is on its way
tower.support.sentBody: It has gone to the buyer’s app and to the store. Nobody here sees it, including you — that is what makes it worth anything.
tower.support.otpBody: A peer send has no app to receive a code, so this one is shown here — once. It is not stored anywhere you can read it again.
tower.support.proofHint: What a dispute would be judged against
tower.pictures.title: Pictures for the pickers
tower.pictures.lede: A drawing of “a flatbed” is a claim about what trucks look like HERE. The network ships a picture for every option; upload your own wherever it does not match what arrives at your counters.
tower.pictures.topic.bodyHint: what turns up to carry it
tower.pictures.topic.equipmentHint: what lifts it on and off
tower.pictures.saved: Saved — {key}. Every picker asking about this now shows it.
tower.pictures.reverted: Reverted — {key} shows the network’s drawing again.
tower.pictures.notAnImage: That file could not be read as an image.
tower.pictures.footer: Shown on every picker that asks for these. Pictures are scaled down here before they are uploaded, so a clerk on a slow connection is not paying for a photograph. The WORDING lives in the app translations, not here.
tower.stores.title: Stores
tower.stores.lede: Every store that ships through the network. Find one by the name it gives on the phone, then open it to see what the call is likely about: whether it has float, whether a payment arrived, and whether its systems are answering.
tower.stores.noneFound: No store matches “{query}”. A store is found by its name, its store number, its street, its country or the company of ours it pays.
tower.stores.readFailed: The stores could not be read. Try again.
tower.stores.nothingWrongLede: Nothing on this store’s record looks wrong: no label is waiting on its float, no payment is outstanding, and nothing sent to its systems has been given up on.
tower.stores.says.unpaid: Shipments not paid for: {unpaid}. Their labels are held back, and print by themselves once its float covers them. It pays in from the Store app.
tower.stores.says.awaited: Payments it started that have not arrived: {open}. When the money is in the account, confirm it under Money in, by the reference below.
tower.stores.says.failing: Messages to its systems given up on after eight tries: {failed}. The reason for each is below, in our words. The address is theirs to put right, in the Store app.
tower.stores.says.returns: Parcels offered back to it and not yet answered: {returns}. It answers in the Store app; an offer nobody answers runs out.
tower.stores.signIn.account: With an email and password of its own.
tower.stores.signIn.secret: With its store number and signing secret: it has not set up an account yet. The Store app asks it to the next time somebody signs in.
tower.stores.signIn.rotated: Its signing secret was last replaced {date}.
tower.stores.dockNone: None: it drops off at a shop.
tower.stores.rating: {average} from {count, plural, one {# rating} other {# ratings}}
tower.stores.noTillLede: No company of ours operates a till in {country}, so this store holds no float with the network and is billed nothing by it.
tower.stores.noEntries: Nothing has been paid in or billed yet.
tower.stores.recentHint: Its last five entries. The whole register is the store’s own, in the Store app.
tower.stores.shipmentCounts: {total} in all · {active} on the way · {unpaid} not paid for
tower.stores.parcelHint: Its newest five. To see where one is, look it up by its number under Find a parcel.
tower.stores.noShipments: It has not shipped anything yet.
tower.stores.returnsWaiting: Offered back to it and waiting on its answer: {n}.
tower.stores.cbCounts: {delivered} arrived · {pending} still owed · {failed} given up on
tower.stores.cbTo: Its systems are told about its parcels at
tower.stores.cbCarries: The message that a parcel is ready carries the buyer’s collection code.
tower.stores.cbCarriesNot: The store has switched the collection code off: it never leaves the network that way.
tower.stores.cbNone: No address is set, so nothing is sent to software of its own. Its people see every parcel in the Store app all the same; a store that has systems sets the address there.
tower.stores.noKeys: It has made no keys: nothing of its own calls the network.
tower.stores.readOnly: You read here and change nothing. A store changes its own address, keys and settings in the Store app; its buyers, their collection codes and its signing secret are not shown to staff.
tower.ids.title: ID disputes
tower.ids.lede: Two people say one national ID number is theirs: one holds it on their registration, the other was refused. Each sends three photographs of themselves with their card and their reference. One of us says whose it is and why; a second, different one approves. Whoever does not get it keeps their account, and can still come in person.
tower.ids.waitingNone: No dispute is waiting on us.
tower.ids.unread: That dispute could not be read just now.
tower.ids.row.opened: the claimant’s photographs are due by {date}
tower.ids.who.none: No registration yet: they were refused
tower.ids.who.unknown: A registration with nobody signed in behind it
tower.ids.fact.appointmentOffDay: The company no longer receives visitors then: it changed its days, its hours or its closed dates. Both tickets say so, and the person who made the appointment can choose again.
tower.ids.fact.reminded: Whoever of the two has an account was reminded on {when}, in the app and by email, with what to bring.
tower.ids.fact.willRemind: Whoever of the two has an account is reminded the day before, in the app and by email, with what to bring.
tower.ids.place.perHour: {n, plural, one {# visitor} other {# visitors}} an hour
tower.ids.place.noDays: No visiting days set, so a person may choose any day and is told to ask first
tower.ids.place.theirs: The address, the visiting days and hours, the dates it is closed and how many visitors it sees in an hour are the country’s own company’s to set: signed in to this console as that company, under Settings, How to reach you. We do not type them here. Until it has, a ticket says to ask staff.
tower.ids.fact.referenceHint: It should be handwritten on paper in their first picture. A picture without it was not taken for this.
tower.ids.fact.reason: The reason the other one will read
tower.ids.numbersHint: The ID number itself is never shown here, and nor is a whole phone number. You type the number you read on a card and are told whether it is the disputed one.
tower.ids.photos: {n, plural, one {# photograph} other {# photographs}} sent for this
tower.ids.noPhotos: They have sent no photographs yet.
tower.ids.noPhotosHolder: The holder has sent no photographs. If their week is over, it can be decided without them.
tower.ids.readLabel: The number you read on this card
tower.ids.readHint: Typed exactly as it is on the card. It is not kept: only whether it is the disputed number.
tower.ids.retakeLabel: Ask for these photographs again, because
tower.ids.retakeHint: Blurred, glare on the card, no reference in the picture. They read this, their photographs are deleted, and they have another week.
tower.ids.retakeCta: Ask them to take the photographs again
tower.ids.note.holderSilent: The holder sent nothing in their week. If the claimant’s card carries the number, the ID can go to them. The holder’s registration is then held, not removed.
tower.ids.note.claimantDiffers: The claimant’s own card carries a different number. They typed somebody else’s when they registered: the ID stays where it is, and they register with the number on their card.
tower.ids.note.holderDiffers: The holder’s own card carries a different number: theirs was mistyped. If the ID goes to the claimant, the holder’s record takes the number you read and nobody is held.
tower.ids.note.bothMatch: Both cards carry this number, so one of them is not genuine, and a photograph cannot always say which. Compare each face with its card, the reference in each first picture, and what the holder sent when they registered. If you cannot tell, leave it with the holder and say so: whoever does not get it can come in with the card itself.
tower.ids.note.nothingOnRecord: The holder sent no copy of an ID when they registered, so there is nothing older to compare their photographs with.
tower.ids.wait.opened: Waiting for the claimant’s photographs. The holder has not been told yet.
tower.ids.wait.answering: The holder has been told and has a week to answer. It can be decided when they have, or when the week is over.
tower.ids.wait.appointment: An appointment is made. What is seen there is recorded from that day.
tower.ids.over: Nothing is left to decide here.
tower.ids.proposeLede: Read the number on each card first. Then say whose ID it is. Nothing changes until a second member of staff approves it.
tower.ids.recordLede: The day of the appointment has come. Say who came, read the number on each card you were shown, and say whose ID it is. A second member of staff approves it, and that is final.
tower.ids.came.claimant: The one who was refused came, with their card
tower.ids.came.holder: The one who holds it came, with their card
tower.ids.cannot.claimantCard: Read the number on the claimant’s card first. The ID can only go to somebody whose card carries it.
tower.ids.cannot.holderCard: The holder has shown no card carrying this number, and the claimant’s card has not been read as carrying a different one. Read the cards first.
tower.ids.cannot.notCame: The decision can change only for somebody who came with their card.
tower.ids.means.claimant: The ID is kept for the one who was refused until they register. The holder’s registration is held: they finish what they have in hand and start nothing new until an ID of their own is on record.
tower.ids.means.claimantCorrected: The ID is kept for the one who was refused until they register. The holder’s record takes the number you read on their own card, and nothing else changes for them.
tower.ids.means.holder: Nothing changes for the holder. The one who was refused is told why, and can still make an appointment.
tower.ids.whatHint: The face against the card, the reference in the picture, what is on record. The second member of staff approves on the strength of it.
tower.ids.reason: The reason, for the one who does not get it
tower.ids.reasonHint: They read this with their reference. Say what they can do next.
tower.ids.otherApproves: You proposed this one. The approval is a second member of staff’s to give.
tower.ids.approveLede: Approving gives the ID as proposed and tells both people. Whoever does not get it has two weeks to make an appointment.
tower.ids.approveFinalLede: Approving makes this final and tells both people. If it differs from the first decision, the ID changes hands again.
tower.ids.sendBackHint: It returns to be looked at again. Whoever proposes next reads this.
tower.ids.effect.corrected: The holder’s record took the number on their own card.
tower.ids.final.changed: The decision changed: now for {who} — approved by {by}, {when}.
tower.moves.title: Account moves
tower.moves.lede: Somebody who has lost their phone number, forgotten their PIN and cannot read their recovery email has no way back into their account by themselves. Two of us can move it to a new number: one checks who is asking and writes down what they checked, a second approves. It is also exactly what somebody after another person’s account would ask for — so check first, and read what the account says against them.
tower.moves.waitingNone: Nobody is waiting for an account to be moved.
tower.moves.unread: That request could not be read just now.
tower.moves.rowSub: From a number ending {from} to one ending {to} · asked {when}
tower.moves.fact.to: The number to move it to
tower.moves.fact.endsProved: Ends {ends} — they confirmed it with a code
tower.moves.numbersHint: No whole phone number is shown, here or anywhere: ask the person for both numbers and compare the last three digits.
tower.moves.id.matches: It is the one this account registered with
tower.moves.id.differs: It is NOT the one this account registered with
tower.moves.id.none_on_record: They typed one, and this account has none on record
tower.moves.noAccount: The number they gave names no account, so there is nothing to move. Refuse it with a reason they can act on — and do not tell them whether that number has an account: the person asking may not be its owner.
tower.moves.warn.pinUsed: This account’s PIN was used at {when} — after this was asked. The person asking said they had lost it. Checking or approving will stop the request instead of moving the account.
tower.moves.warn.idDiffers: The national ID they typed is not the one this account registered with.
tower.moves.warn.numberChanged: This account’s number was already changed at {when}, and that can still be undone. It cannot be moved again until that is settled.
tower.moves.warn.nothingToCheck: This account only sends and collects parcels: we hold no ID for it and no name outside the vault. There is little to check anybody against — ask what they sent or collected lately, and from where.
tower.moves.warn.hasEmail: It has a recovery email, {email}. Ask why they cannot read it: with it they could get back in without us.
tower.moves.ended.stoppedHolder: Stopped {when}: somebody signed in to the account said it was not them
tower.moves.ended.stoppedPin: Stopped {when}: the account’s PIN was used after this was asked
tower.moves.ended.lapsed: Lapsed {when}: nobody decided it in time
tower.moves.checkLede: You are the first of two. Check who is asking — see their ID where the account has one on record, ask what only its owner would know — and write down what you checked. Nothing moves yet: a second member of staff approves on the strength of what you write.
tower.moves.checkHint: For example: “Saw their national ID card at the Nairobi office; the number matches.” It is kept with the request.
tower.moves.approveLede: {who} checked who is asking. If what they wrote satisfies you, approve: the account moves to the number ending {ends} at once and every phone signed in to it is signed out. Its holder is told, and for 24 hours can undo it with the old number and the PIN as it was.
tower.moves.otherApproves: You checked this one. The approval is a second member of staff’s to give.
tower.moves.refuseWhy: Refuse it: why (the person who asked reads this)
tower.moves.refuseHint: Say what they can do next. Do not say whether the number has an account, or anything about it.
tower.biz.title: Businesses
tower.gs1.title: A GS1 prefix disputed
tower.gs1.waiting: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing waiting} one {One waiting} other {# waiting}}
tower.gs1.lede: A business says a GS1 company prefix another business uses is its own. Read both licences: the prefix and the company it is licensed to are on each. One of you says whose it is and why; another approves. Decided for the one who asked, the others stop printing under it, and their loads keep the codes they were given.
tower.gs1.step.waiting: Waiting for the licence of {names}, until {by}.
tower.gs1.step.ready: Every licence is in, or the week is over: say whose it is.
tower.gs1.step.proposed: {by} says the prefix is {whose}’s. A second member of staff approves or sends it back.
tower.gs1.step.decided: The prefix is {whose}’s: said by {proposedBy}, approved by {by} on {at}.
tower.gs1.forwarder: a client of {name}, who answers for it
tower.gs1.store: a store, answering in the Store app
tower.gs1.whyBack: Why it goes back (to send it back)
tower.gs1.notYou: You said whose it is: a second member of staff approves.
tower.biz.lede: Shippers, importers, expeditors, clearing agents and yards sign themselves up and work straight away. What waits for you is being shown to strangers: a public page and a place in the agent finder. Check the registration certificate against the name and number they gave, and the ID of the person speaking for them. Then two of you approve.
tower.biz.waitingNone: Nobody is waiting for a check.
tower.biz.papersLede: The certificate must name {name} and carry the number {reg}. The ID must be of a person the certificate or a letter on it says may speak for the business.
tower.biz.paper.waiting: Added by {who} on {when} — not verified yet.
tower.biz.paper.rejectWhy: Why not — the business reads this
